title: Hambroodjes (Ham Bread Croquettes)
description: A bread preparation made with ham, bread, and veal.

ingredients.name: 1 to 1.5 dl water with salt or stock
ingredients.sourceText: 1 to 1.5 dl water with salt or stock

steps: Grind the ham and meat together.
Prepare the sauce as described in recipe 102 and mix the meat with it.
Add salt and pepper if needed.
Cut thin slices of old bread, remove the crusts and make the pieces equal in shape.
Spread them with a thick layer of the mixture, so that it lies higher in the middle than at the edges.
Beat the eggs, soak the bread rolls in them until they are completely absorbed, drip the top repeatedly with the egg.
Roll them through fine breadcrumbs and fry them brown in hot salad oil.
Let them drain on gray paper and place them on a small plate on which a folded cloth lies.

title: Hangop (Curdled Milk Dessert)
description: Prepared with buttermilk, rusks, and brown sugar.
steps: Place a cloth rinsed in clean water in a colander, set it in a deep bowl and pour the buttermilk into it
Let the watery part of the buttermilk drain off
From time to time scoop the thick part out of the cloth and continue until the hangop is completely drained
Beat the hangop smooth and stir, if the hangop is too sour, some milk or cream through it
Serve it with brown sugar and rusks or with cornflakes

title: Haringsla (Herring Salad)
description: A salad made with herrings, apples, and beet.

ingredients.name: 1 head of lettuce or 1 bunch of curly endive or 100 g field lettuce
ingredients.sourceText: 1 head of lettuce or 1 bunch of curly endive or 100 g field lettuce

steps: Clean the herrings as indicated in recipe 5. Cut them into small pieces.
Boil the egg hard (8 minutes), peel it, separate the white from the yolk and mash both separately.
Peel and mince the apples, mash the potatoes.
Clean the lettuce, cut it finely, wash it and squeeze it as dry as possible.
Peel the cooked beet, cut it into slices of approximately 1/4 cm thickness and cut these into small cubes.
Mix most of all these ingredients together, but reserve a small part for garnish, except for the apples as they discolor quickly.
Stir in oil and vinegar or some mayonnaise to taste and some pepper and salt.
Lay this mixture on a plate, smooth it, but ensure it is slightly higher in the middle than at the edges.
Use the remainder as garnish and lay it on in sections or stripes, ensuring the underlying mixture is completely covered.
Further garnish the plate with onions and gherkins.
Note: The egg can also be cut into quarters or sixths and used only as garnish.

title: Hazenpastei (Hare Pâté)
description: Prepared with hare, veal, and bacon.
steps: Remove all bones from the hare, cut the meat into pieces, wash it and place it for 24 hours in half water, half vinegar with the spices.
Dry the nice pieces from back and thigh, cut them into thin slices and lard these with very thin strips of bacon.
Grind the washed meat and bacon twice through the meat grinder, do the same with the remaining pieces of hare and mix this mass with pepper, salt and nutmeg to taste.
Choose a pâté pot that can be completely filled with this quantity.
Cover the bottom and side walls with thin slices of bacon, arrange first a layer of the slices, place a layer of meat mixture on top and continue until everything is used up.
Pour the marinade mixed with some bouillon over it until the mass is covered.
Close the pot with the lid and brush the edge with a paste of flour and water.
Place the pâté in a fairly warm oven and let it stand there for approximately 3 hours.
Loosen the lid, pour a layer of melted lard over it, close the pot again and seal the edge of lid and pot with foil.
Store the pâté in a cool place.

title: IJspudding (Ice Pudding)
description: A pudding made with coffee, fruits, and vanilla.
steps: Make vanilla and coffee ice cream in the known manner (see recipe 880 and recipe 883).
Then divide an ice mold, either with tins or with cardboard plates, into vertical parts, carefully fill these with the ice cream types, remove the partitions.
Press the ice cream as firmly as possible.
Close the mold well, for example with a strip of surgical tape, so that no salt water can enter.
Place it in a bucket in which finely crushed raw ice and salt have been added.
Wrap the bucket in one or more blankets or molton cloths.
Let the pudding stand like this for at least 2 hours.
If the raw ice has already largely melted, then it is necessary to remove the water and refill the remainder with newly crushed ice and salt.
After the indicated time, remove the mold from the bucket and rinse it with cold water to prevent salt water from entering.
Hold it just before turning out in very lukewarm water.
The pudding then comes loose from the mold and can be easily turned out.
This is done on a chilled plate.
Quickly garnish the pudding with halved French candied fruits and if desired whipped cream.
Serve it immediately and provide waffle cookies.

title: Kabinetpudding (Cold) (8 persons)
description: Prepared with vanilla pod or vanilla or sugar, rum, and currants.

ingredients.name: ½ vanilla pod or vanilla sugar

ingredients.name: white gelatin or 30 g powdered gelatin

steps: Remove the stems from the currants and raisins, rinse them with lukewarm water, cover with boiling water and cook for 10 minutes. Let them drain well in a sieve.
Chop the candied citron finely.
Beat the egg yolks with the sugar vigorously together, add as much of the milk mixed with the vanilla that has been brought to a boil until they are thoroughly warmed and the sugar is dissolved.
Return everything to the pan, let it bind in a bain-marie while stirring well, but ensure it does not boil.
Remove the mass from the heat and stir in the soaked gelatin, mixed dried fruit and rum or arak.

Let the mixture cool, stirring occasionally, add the stiffly beaten egg whites, let everything together, also stirring occasionally, become jelly-like and pour it into a pudding mold rinsed with unbeaten egg white.
Let the pudding cool and set firmly, turn it out onto a damp plate and serve without sauce.
Note: The pudding mold rinsed with egg white can be garnished with strips of angelica and candied fruit pieces.

Turn it in the iron pot from time to time.

Serve with compote.

title: Kastanjesoep (Chestnut Soup)

steps: Wash the chestnuts, make a cross on them, set them with enough boiling water so they just cover and let them cook for 10 minutes

title: Kerstbrood or Weihnachtsstolle (Christmas Bread or Christmas Stollen)
description: A bread preparation made with yeast, egg yolk, and butter or margarine.
steps: Make bread dough as described for white bread (recipe 835) from flour, yeast, salt, egg and milk.
Let it rise.

Then mix in the washed and dried currants and raisins with the finely cut candied peel, the snipped almonds and orange peel strips, the melted butter or margarine, the sugar, the cinnamon, the grated lemon peel.
Put the dough in a greased bread pan or let it rise covered in a bowl for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Bake the bread in the pan as described for white bread.
For a true Weihnachtsstolle, flatten the dough and give it the shape of a round cake.
Fold it double, but make sure the bottom half is larger than the top.
Press the dough well together.
Let it rise covered on a greased baking sheet for a while.
Bake the stollen as indicated for white bread (see recipe 835).
Dust it with sifted powdered sugar.
Tie a red ribbon around it and stick a sprig of holly between.

title: Ketelkoek (Kettle Cake)
description: A cake made with currants, yeast, and flour.

ingredients.name: currants, raisins and candied citrus peel
ingredients.sourceText: 150 g currants, raisins and candied citrus peel

steps: Put the flour in a bowl, add the egg and lukewarm milk and stir out the lumps from this batter.
Add the well-washed currants and raisins, which have been stripped of their stems, the chopped candied citrus peel, the salt, and lastly the yeast mixed with a little lukewarm milk.
Let the batter rise, covered, in a lukewarm place (1/2 hour to 3/4 hour).
Grease the inside of a hot pudding mold with butter (also the lid) and sprinkle it with fine breadcrumbs.
Put the batter in it, but make sure the mold is only filled 2/3 to 3/4.
Close the mold firmly and cook the pudding about 2 hours in a water bath, but make sure the water is constantly filled to just below the rim of the pudding mold.
Check if the pudding is done by inserting a knitting needle, which must come out dry.
Let it dry without the lid and serve the pudding with butter or margarine and syrup or sugar, or if preferred with a syrup sauce.

description: Prepared with chicken, butter or margarine, and salt.

ingredients.name: boter of margarine (butter or margarine)
ingredients.sourceText: 80 g boter of margarine (butter or margarine)

steps: Was de kip met lauw water af of veeg ze met een vochtig doekje van binnen en van buiten schoon, wrijf ze in met wat zout.
Strooi ook binnenin wat zout en doe er een stukje boter of margarine in.
Maak de rest in de braadslede of een stoofpan lichtbruin, leg hierin de kip, bedruip ze aan alle kanten met het hete vet en braad ze lichtbruin en gaar (5 kwartier), sluit de pan.
Keer de kip, wanneer ze in een stoofpan gebraden wordt, telkens om en voeg er zo nodig wat water bij als boter of margarine dreigt bruin te worden.
Bedruip de kippen, wanneer ze in een braadslede gebraden worden, dikwijls en leg zo nodig een ingevet stuk wit papier op de borsten, wanneer deze te bruin worden.
Probeer of de kip gaar is, door met een vork tussen de gewrichten te prikken; deze moet er dan gemakkelijk doorgaan.
Maak de jus op de gewone wijze af met water.
Leg de getrancheerde kip op een schaal, giet er wat jus over, maak manchetjes aan de poten, geef er gestoofde vruchten of sla bij.

title: Konijnensoep (Rabbit Soup)
description: A soup made with rabbit, rabbits, and onions.
steps: Take one or two rabbits from which you have saved the blood for thickening. After they are well cleaned, cut them into pieces and let them brown slightly in butter, parsley and sliced onions. Add some salt and pepper.
When the rabbit pieces are well colored, make a roux of 1.5 hectograms flour, 1 glass of red wine and 3 liters of water.
Let the rabbits become done, and when done, pour them through a strainer, clean each piece well, taking care that no small bone fragments remain.
Put all the rabbit pieces in a pot. Let the cooking liquid simmer gently on the side of the stove so you can skim it well. Keep the rabbit pieces warm.

After the cooking liquid has simmered gently for half an hour, add Liebig's Meat Extract to it and thicken it with the blood, after you have skimmed off the foam. Place the rabbit pieces (without heads) in the soup tureen, pour the cooking liquid over with a little Cayenne pepper.

title: Koolsoep (Cabbage Soup)
description: A soup made with cabbage, bacon, and carrots.
steps: Remove the outer leaves of the savoy cabbage as they are usually tough, cut the cabbage into 4 pieces, and wash them in plenty of water.
Boil them for 10 minutes with 2 hectograms of lean bacon in boiling water.
Then place them for one hour in plenty of cold water. Through this treatment you will have made the cabbage easily digestible.
Take the cabbage and carefully press all the water out, then season each piece with some salt and pepper.

title: Leverworst (Liver Sausage)
description: Prepared with pork or veal liver, pork, and bacon.
steps: Cook the cleaned liver, cleaned meat and neck bacon for 5 hours in plenty of boiling salted water.
Grind everything as finely as possible, mix it with the spices, salt, broth and very finely chopped onions.
Clean the casings, which have been soaked in lukewarm water for some time, thoroughly and stuff the meat through a sausage horn into the casings, not too tightly.
Prick occasionally with a needle while stuffing and tie the sausages closed at both ends.
Cook them in plenty of boiling salted water until they float to the surface (approximately 15 to 20 minutes), but let them cook very gently so they do not burst.
Let them cool completely, lying side by side.
Note: If you wish to keep the sausage for a while, let it smoke very lightly.

The easiest way to fill the casings is to place the sausage horn on the meat grinder with the blade removed, then pass the mixture through the grinder. The casing, which is stretched over the sausage horn, fills evenly but must be supported by hand.

title: Louisepudding (Louise Pudding)
description: A pudding made with bread, egg yolks, and egg whites.
steps: Make the bread, freed of crusts, fine in the boiling milk, so there are no lumps
Add the butter or margarine
Stir the egg yolks with the sugar and grated lemon zest
Add the bread with the butter or margarine to this
Fold in the two stiffly beaten egg whites as lightly as possible at the end
Grease a warm pudding mold (also the lid) with some butter or margarine, dust it with powdered sugar and add the mixture, but ensure the mold is filled only 3/4 full
Close the mold firmly and cook it 1.5 hours au bain-marie, but ensure the water is always refilled to just below the rim of the mold
Let the pudding dry out a little without the lid

Turn it out onto a fireproof dish and quickly coat it with the jam and then with the two stiffly beaten egg whites with sugar, sprinkle some sugar over it and quickly place it in a hot oven to brown it lightly
Garnish the pudding afterwards with strips of angelica and the candied fruits, which should already be ready
Bring the pudding to the table as hot as possible and serve with warm vanilla sauce or wine sauce

title: Marsepein (Marzipan)
description: Prepared with almonds, powdered sugar, and egg white.

ingredients.name: a few drops of lemon juice
ingredients.sourceText: a few drops of lemon juice

ingredients.name: optionally some rose or orange blossom water
ingredients.sourceText: optionally some rose or orange blossom water

steps: Peel the soaked almonds, wash and dry them and grind them in the almond mill.
Mix them with the sifted powdered sugar, the unbeaten egg white, the drops of lemon juice and the rose or orange blossom water.
Mill this mass through a mill (with the finest blade) and catch the first portion separately, because it may have a less beautiful white color.
Knead the coming fine, white dough thoroughly together and let it rest 24 hours in a damp cloth.
Then the marzipan can be processed in various ways. For example, add some orange essence through the mass, if small root vegetables are to be made.
To make small potatoes, roll round balls of the dough through some cinnamon and prick it here and there.
Color some portions for example with cacao powder or with plant colorants.
Roll each portion into a sheet on a table dusted with some powdered sugar and stick them together with some water.
Roll them together once more and cut or stamp cookies from them.
Garnish them with a half hazelnut, almond or walnut.

title: Mayonnaise (First Recipe)
description: Prepared with egg or egg yolks, salad oil, and vinegar.
steps: Stir the egg or egg yolks with mustard, salt and pepper for 10 minutes with a good tinned whisk.

Store in a jar under a layer of oil.
